**Memorandum: Explaining Divergent Projections on the Clean-Energy Tax Credit Expansion**

Prepared on behalf of the energy industry coalition to support committee review, this nonpartisan explainer outlines why forecasts for the clean-energy tax credit expansion diverge so sharply across different economic models. Reputable studies produce varying fiscal and emissions estimates largely because they rely on differing assumptions regarding future technology costs, supply chain bottlenecks, macroeconomic conditions, and the actual utilization rates of these uncapped tax credits. While experts broadly agree that the incentives will accelerate renewable energy deployment and lower overall emissions, there is genuine disagreement regarding the final budgetary cost to taxpayers and whether the credits will drive lasting technological innovation or merely subsidize mature industries. Furthermore, current analyses highlight regional and distributional equity questions, indicating that investments may disproportionately flow to states with existing clean-energy infrastructure, and that lower utility costs will only reach low-income households if developers pass down their tax savings. Members can use this framework to objectively probe hearing witnesses on the specific economic variables driving their varying forecasts and the potential localized impacts of the proposed expansion.
